sheets.inspection: Full 1536x1024 output opened at original detail, without downscaling; all six poses inspected.

findings.observation: Two fine supported forelegs and partly occluded rear feet connect below real chest. Broad-rooted cupped ears, dark eye rims, projecting pale muzzle and irregular bib correspond to N29/N19; head remains modest.

Continuous shoulder/ribcage/pelvis with belly volume, credible hind hock bend and four owned feet. Rump ends in tiny near-flush nub rather than extended tail. Smooth outline now matches N19/N27, fine pen texture does not create a mane.
Far-side occlusion coherent, fine legs support full trunk, ears remain triangular and cream stops before high socks. No disconnected paw or surplus limb.

Deep chest, dark throat between tan chest fields, visible substantial leg shafts and clearance correspond to B04/B23. Pale moustache, brow arcs and pendant ear furnishings remain regional rather than whole-body shag.

Neck connects head and shoulder; dark trunk extends continuously to haunch without sausage or square-terrier proportions. Four support points readable. Tapering dark tail with modest fringe is compatible with B29; exact neutral proportions cannot be measured from B29 stride.
Foreshortened torso retains length and full chest; far feet behind near supports are unambiguous. Face grooming corresponds to B04/B26 qualitatively, without treating hair width as skull width.

Consistent restrained ink/watercolor, clean negative space, readable labels, no stray anatomy or visual contamination found at native resolution. This is a model test; story scene fidelity/comedy remain to be checked in each illustration.

limitations: Drawn proportions are provisional qualitative interpretations of uncalibrated views.
Fine texture and light wash vary from literal photo color; no measured palette is claimed.
A clear model does not clear subsequent scene outputs.

sheets.inspection: Opened full output at native1536x1024; both vignettes inspected against original N19/N25/B29/B19/B12 and native detail crops.

findings.observation: Extended forelegs connect through shoulders to full narrow torso, folded haunch attached and resting on rug. Fine smooth coat and cupped broad-rooted ears correspond to N25/N19; no extra leg or long tail.

Head rests between owned front paws, shoulders continue into elongated trunk and folded near haunch. Dark back remains close coated while face/ear furnishings follow B19. Raised rear contour is a tucked pose under perspective, not disconnected head/torso. Do not use this view for neutral standing ratios.
Four fine planted legs connect through full body, projecting muzzle and broad triangular ears remain recognizable; short smooth nub is visible, not long tail.

Two flexed forelegs clearly rooted at chest and two grounded hindfeet below attached pelvis; raised open jaw around orange ball matches B12 action intent. Clipped ear/head state is explicitly photo-grounded B12 variation. Tail dark/tapering, torso full and continuous.

findings.result: No material defect in sheet; additional model scope required
findings.observation: Dogs share ground planes and consistent pen/wash finish in both rows. No merged anatomy, contamination or unexplained extra objects. sheets.inspection: Opened whole sheet at native1536x1024 and compared both subjects to previously opened N19/N29/B04/B29 originals and native details.

findings.observation: Both dogs stand in same shallow three-quarter ground plane; each has four distinguishable owned feet and shadows. No merged legs or floating support; slight near/far paw offsets agree with perspective.
Fine long limbs, real ribcage/haunch, visible neck, large cupped triangular ears and projecting pale muzzle retained. Rump has near-flush short nub. Coat outline smooth; no mane or high socks.

Continuous moderately elongated charcoal torso, full chest, visible neck and substantial leg clearance maintained. Moustache, brows, ear fringe and pale lower legs regional; face modest beside trunk. Tail remains dark and tapering with modest fringe.

Compatible with standing v002 design; no unexpected head enlargement, anatomy duplication or visual contamination found. Restrained expressions can support later situational acting without already prescribing a story.

limitations: Relative scale is an illustrative continuity choice and unmeasured; this is not owner-adopted size canon.
Whole-sheet pen texture is an illustration, not literal coat photometry.

sheets.inspection: Actual sheet opened complete at native1448×1086; compared to original N19/N29/B04/B29/B26 evidence already inspected with native detail crops.
findings: Flatter torso color planes are effective; remaining low-relief paint/paper grain does not alone imply longer fur. Both dogs have connected full trunks, four owned grounded limbs and distinct heads/ears.
Neet lateral neck behind jaw and white bib edges project pointed fur tufts, contradicting very short smooth neck coat. Smooth these contours.

Buddy lower chest/belly margin shows pointed fringe; tail is raised thick brush with upturned feathery tip. Require close underbody margin and slender natural lowered/extended taper, preserving regional face/ear furnishing.
limitations: Supplementary finish reference only; does not replace originals as anatomical authority or calibrate relative size.

sheets.inspection: Complete actual replacement opened native1448×1086 and compared to v003 and original-photo evidence.
findings: Neet lateral neck outer silhouette now continuous and close rather than projecting tufts; irregular pale bib remains internal marking. Tiny rump nub and four fine connected legs preserved.

Buddy tail now lowered near horizontal with slender taper and no brush-tip plume. Underbody silhouette simplified; remaining tiny edge irregularities do not create floor-length shag or materially alter clipped torso.

Full continuous torsos, owned four paws each and ground support preserved. Smooth broad painted planes establish useful supplementary finish direction; nondirectional wash grain acceptable. Buddy face and pendant ears retain localized furnishing.
limitations: Only supplementary finish interpretation, never anatomical authority; no calibrated relative scale, breed or movement timing.
